## Existing work we built on

Four lines of work shaped the project: they set the question, the baselines, the metrics and the tests.

> **Explain it:** Traders and researchers believe dealer hedging moves markets; volatility forecasters know simple HAR models are hard to beat; and set models like DeepSets and attention can read a variable-size option chain. We put the three together and tested them with the evaluation rules the forecasting literature recommends.

| Area | Work | What we took from it |
|---|---|---|
| Dealer hedging moves prices | Ni, Pearson, Poteshman & White (2021), *Review of Financial Studies* 34(4) | Option market-maker hedging raises the volatility and the chance of large moves of the underlying: the reason GEX could matter |
| | Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021), *Journal of Financial Economics* 142(1) | Hedging short gamma trades with the price move and creates intraday momentum; stronger when negative gamma exposure is larger |
| | Barbon & Buraschi, "Gamma Fragility" (working paper, 2020–21) | Large dealer gamma imbalances go with intraday momentum, reversals and fragility |
| | Practitioner GEX (dealer gamma exposure) summaries | The one-number summary we test against: gamma × open interest × spot² × 1%, summed over the chain |
| Volatility forecasting | Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys (2003), *Econometrica* | Realized volatility from intraday returns as the measure of what happened |
| | Corsi (2009), *Journal of Financial Econometrics* | HAR-RV: daily, weekly and monthly volatility; our main classical baseline |
| | Christensen, Siggaard & Veliyev (2023), *Journal of Financial Econometrics*; Audrino & Chassot (2024, "HARd to Beat") | Machine learning can improve on HAR, but the gains are modest and a well-fitted HAR is hard to beat: our expectation for the size of any gain |
| Models for sets and sequences | Zaheer et al. (2017), Deep Sets; Vaswani et al. (2017), attention; Lee et al. (2019), Set Transformer | Reading a variable-size, unordered set of contracts: DeepSets, self-attention and attention pooling |
| | Cho et al. (2014), GRU; Ke et al. (2017), LightGBM | The recurrent layer over snapshots and the tuned tree baseline |
| Fair evaluation | Patton (2011), *Journal of Econometrics* | QLIKE and MSE rank volatility forecasts correctly even with a noisy volatility proxy |
| | Diebold & Mariano (1995); Holm (1979); López de Prado (2018) | Comparing forecast errors, correcting for several tests, and walk-forward splits with embargo and purge |

**What was new here:** an auditable point-in-time NIFTY option-chain pipeline, every contract as a token, and a test of GEX against attention models under rules fixed in advance. To our knowledge this comparison has not been published for NIFTY (say "to our knowledge": we did not run a systematic review).

## Every model we ran, and how the metrics changed

Attention + GRU performs as well as the best classical models: it ranks next-day volatility on par with HAR-RV, HAR + GEX and tuned LightGBM (IC 0.447) and clearly better than persistence. On forecast error it has the lowest RMSE of all 8 models (0.285), significantly lower than persistence by 23% (p < 0.001) and tuned LightGBM by 5% (p 0.015); and the lowest QLIKE of all 8 models (0.189), significantly lower than persistence by 50% (p < 0.001), HAR + GEX by 19% (p 0.033) and tuned LightGBM by 16% (p 0.042). The best setup overall is the exploratory HAR-IV + chain correction: IC 0.515, RMSE 0.270, QLIKE 0.186.

> **Explain it:** We built the models as a ladder, each adding one ability, so every step shows what it adds. RMSE and QLIKE measure the size of the misses (lower is better); IC measures whether calm and wild days are put in the right order (higher is better).

![Every next-day model: IC and RMSE](../outputs/reports/figures/study_models_progress.png)

### The main ladder (pre-registered, next day)

| Step | Model | What it does | IC | RMSE | QLIKE | IC vs HAR | RMSE vs HAR | QLIKE vs HAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Historical mean | Always forecasts the training average | — | 0.331 | 0.309 | — | +15.4% | +38.8% |
| 0 | Persistence | Tomorrow is like today | 0.261 | 0.370 | 0.376 | — | +28.9% | +68.6% |
| 1 | HAR-RV | Linear model on daily, weekly and monthly past volatility | 0.434 | 0.287 | 0.223 | — | — | — |
| 2 | HAR + GEX | HAR plus total GEX under three sign conventions | 0.445 | 0.289 | 0.231 | +0.011 | +0.9% | +3.8% |
| 3 | Tuned LightGBM | Decision trees on about 40 summary features | 0.448 | 0.299 | 0.225 | +0.013 | +4.3% | +0.7% |
| 4 | DeepSets | Reads every contract, then a plain average | 0.437 | 0.293 | 0.197 | +0.002 | +2.1% | -11.6% |
| 5 | Self-attention | Contracts compare notes (self-attention), then a learned average | 0.418 | 0.293 | 0.197 | -0.016 | +2.1% | -11.4% |
| 6 | Attention + GRU | Self-attention on 12 snapshots, then a GRU over the hour (ours) | 0.447 | 0.285 | 0.189 | +0.012 | -0.8% | -15.4% |

- **RQ1 (attention + GRU vs the classical rungs):** The pre-registered win rule (a significant IC gain over every classical model) is not met: the IC gains over HAR-RV, HAR + GEX and tuned LightGBM are smaller than the test can detect (gains above +0.060 are ruled out). So the model does well, but not by the clear margin we hoped for.
- **GEX:** Against GEX (HAR + GEX) it ties on ranking (+0.001 IC, 95% interval -0.050 to +0.053) and beats it on forecast error: QLIKE 19% lower (p 0.033); RMSE 1.7% lower, not significant (p 0.29).
- **RQ2:** contracts comparing notes (self-attention vs DeepSets) -0.018 IC (Holm p 0.23); memory of the hour (GRU) +0.028 IC (Holm p 0.2). Neither is significant.

> **Explain it:** HAR is the bar to clear. GEX adds almost nothing to it (+0.011 IC). Our model ties the best on ranking and has the smallest errors: QLIKE 15% below HAR and 19% below HAR + GEX.

### E1: using the chain as a correction (exploratory, next day)

| Model | What it does | IC | RMSE | QLIKE | Test (Holm within E1) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HAR + LightGBM correction | LightGBM on chain-only features predicts HAR's error | 0.481 | 0.280 | 0.219 | +0.046 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.0012 | yes, significant |
| HAR + DeepSets correction | DeepSets on the tokens predicts HAR's error | 0.464 | 0.286 | 0.201 | +0.030 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.037 | yes, significant |
| HAR + attention correction | Self-attention on the tokens predicts HAR's error | 0.477 | 0.278 | 0.196 | +0.042 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.0039 | yes, significant |
| Hybrid | Attention + GRU that sees HAR's forecast and outputs a correction | 0.492 | 0.277 | 0.188 | +0.057 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.012 | yes, significant |
| Combination | Plain average of HAR, LightGBM and attention + GRU | 0.502 | 0.276 | 0.188 | +0.068 IC vs HAR, Holm p < 0.001 | yes, significant |
| State-only control | Same network, volatility numbers only, no contracts | 0.459 | 0.287 | 0.200 | +0.015 IC vs attention + GRU (secondary) | not significant |

> **Explain it:** Instead of asking the network to forecast volatility from scratch, we let HAR forecast and asked the chain what HAR gets wrong. That works: corrections and combinations lift IC from 0.434 to about 0.48–0.50, all significant.

|---|---|---|---|---|

### E3: a new target, volatility over the next 1 and 2 hours (exploratory)

| Model | IC 1 h | RMSE 1 h | IC 2 h | RMSE 2 h |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Persistence | 0.541 | 0.393 | 0.587 | 0.337 |
| Intraday HAR | 0.580 | 0.345 | 0.600 | 0.307 |
| HAR + GEX | 0.577 | 0.346 | 0.597 | 0.308 |
| Tuned LightGBM | 0.582 | 0.363 | 0.597 | 0.328 |
| DeepSets | 0.517 | 0.407 | 0.542 | 0.368 |
| Self-attention | 0.523 | 0.409 | 0.552 | 0.367 |
| Attention + GRU | 0.535 | 0.403 | 0.558 | 0.370 |

Attention + GRU vs the best classical model: 1 h -0.047 IC (Holm p < 0.001), 2 h -0.042 IC (Holm p 0.018): significantly worse. Retraining with the main run's patience (v3 A4) changed nothing.

> **Explain it:** Over the next hour or two, how volatile the market has just been is the best guide, and HAR uses it directly; our reading (not tested) is that the chain mostly adds noise at that horizon.

### v3 checks: separating implied volatility from positioning (exploratory)

| Model | What it does | IC | RMSE | QLIKE | Test (Holm across eight) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HAR-IV | HAR plus the option-implied volatility (ATM IV) | 0.469 | 0.277 | 0.191 | +0.034 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.0079 | yes, significant |
| HAR-IV + chain correction | Chain-only LightGBM corrects HAR-IV | 0.515 | 0.270 | 0.186 | +0.047 IC vs HAR-IV, Holm p 0.005 | yes, significant |
| DeepSets correction, no IV | E1 correction with the IV field removed | 0.460 | 0.289 | 0.216 | +0.025 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.068 | not significant |
| Attention correction, no IV | E1 correction with the IV field removed | 0.474 | 0.282 | 0.210 | +0.039 IC vs HAR, Holm p 0.012 | yes, significant |
| Combination | Average of HAR, LightGBM, attention + GRU | 0.502 | 0.276 | 0.188 | +0.055 IC vs LightGBM, Holm p 0.012 | yes, significant |

> **Explain it:** Implied volatility is a strong input on its own, but the chain still adds information on top of it: the correction improves HAR-IV by +0.047 IC. That is the best result of the project.

## Limitations

What limits these results, grouped so you can answer "what would you do differently?" quickly.

> **Explain it:** Our data access, the size of the sample and what we can observe limit how strong our claims can be. None of these breaks the comparison: every model sees the same data under the same rules.

**Data access**

- **Fixed history window.** The data come from a private archive pulled through a retail broker API (ICICI Direct). The API serves only recent history (about the last six years, per the team), so earlier years cannot be fetched; full historical NIFTY option-chain data is sold to enterprise clients only, not to individual users.
- **Short history per contract.** Each expiry has at most 21 days of option history in the archive, so GEX and the tokens see contracts only near their expiry.
- **Gaps we could not fill.** Option open interest is missing (recorded as 0 by the source) on 69 trading days (2019-07-30, 2022-01-03 to 2022-04-11); daily VIX ends 2026-04-06 (60 trading days without it); spot is missing on 8 days. All are flagged and never imputed.

**What we can observe**

- **Who the dealers are is unknown.** Nobody publishes which side dealers hold, so GEX needs an assumed sign; we tested three conventions (naive, absolute, inferred from previous-day participant data, which covers all index options, not NIFTY alone).
- **Implied volatility cannot be separated fully from the chain.** Gamma, delta and strike GEX are computed from IV, so removing the IV field (v3 A2) still leaves IV inside; v3 A1 is the test that separates them.
- **Tokens come from the nearest expiry only,** and one snapshot time (15:15) is used for the next-day target.

**Sample size and statistics**

- **Few independent test periods.** About 26 walk-forward test periods (under 2,000 labelled days): the paired test detects IC gains of about 0.07 with 80% power, and gains above about +0.06 are ruled out; smaller real gains cannot be confirmed.
- **The rule-change test is weak.** Only 7 test periods fall after November 2024.
- **Realized volatility is itself noisy.** With about 74 five-minute bars a day it misses true volatility by about 0.10 (RMS, on the log scale), so even a perfect forecaster would show an RMSE near that; much lower RMSE is not reachable on this target.
- **Exploratory results are exploratory.** E1–E3 and the v3 checks were registered before their runs but after the main results were known; they explain the main result and do not change RQ1–RQ3.

**Scope**

- **One market and one main horizon:** NIFTY only, next-day volatility for the pre-registered tests (1–2 hours exploratory).
- **No test of economic value:** we measure forecast accuracy, not trading or hedging profit after costs.
- **What attention shows is limited:** we stored only the pooling weights (a near-plain average on all but 4 of 1,552 days); interactions inside the encoder layers were not measured.
- **Devices:** the main neural runs used the Mac GPU, the exploratory ones Explorer V100s; neural models are only compared with each other on the same device.
